dek: Taylor Swift reclaims No. 1 as Tinashe scores her first Billboard 200 top 10.

slides.label: The Comeback
slides.text: Taylor Swift's *The Life of a Showgirl* jumps 21-1 for a *13th* nonconsecutive week at No. 1.

slides.label: The Reissue
slides.text: Sept. 25 drop *The Encore* added 4 new songs: Patient Zero, Cleveland!, Pink Clouding, Babylon.

slides.label: The Numbers
slides.text: 173,000 units moved, up *619%* from the week before. 78% came from streaming.

slides.label: The Gap
slides.text: 9 months between No. 1 weeks, the *longest gap* for a top album since Bad Bunny earlier this year.

slides.label: Tinashe's Moment
slides.text: Elsewhere in the top 10: Tinashe's *Popstar* debuts at No. 6, her first top 10 album ever.

slides.label: 11 Years Later
slides.text: Tinashe charted her first album in *2014*. This is her 7th charted set and biggest sales week yet.

slides.label: Also Top 10
slides.text: Kenny Chesney grabs his *17th* top 10 album as Silver Sands Marina bows at No. 7.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: Hits don't always equal instant recognition. Tinashe's *decade-long climb* shows the grind is real for Black women in music.

question: Tinashe's 11-year wait: patience paid off or industry too slow? One word.
first_comment: Fun fact: Tinashe's 2014 debut Aquarius peaked at No. 17. It took until now to crack the top 10.
photo_caption: Swift's Showgirl hits No. 1 as Tinashe lands first top 10 album
caption_instagram:
Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl is back at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 after its Encore reissue, but the real story in this week's chart is Tinashe. Swift's album jumped 21-1 for a 13th nonconsecutive week on top, boosted by 173,000 units and four new songs added on Sept. 25.

Right behind her, Tinashe's Popstar debuted at No. 6, her first top 10 album ever on the Billboard 200. She first charted in 2014 with Aquarius, which peaked at No. 17. Eleven years, seven albums and a dance hit called No Broke Boys later, she finally broke through.

Kenny Chesney also landed his 17th top 10 set with Silver Sands Marina at No. 7.

Tinashe's 11-year wait: patience paid off or industry too slow? One word.

caption_linkedin:
Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl returned to No. 1 on the Billboard 200 this week after a reissue, marking her 13th nonconsecutive week atop the chart. It's a reminder of how reissues and bonus content can reset momentum in a crowded market.

But the sharper lesson this week comes from Tinashe. Her album Popstar debuted at No. 6, her first top 10 album on the Billboard 200 after 11 years and seven prior releases. The breakthrough followed the slow-burn success of her 2024 track No Broke Boys, which spent 24 weeks at No. 1 on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs before crossing into the Hot 100 top 40.

For independent artists and underrepresented founders alike, the timeline matters. Consistency and staying in the market long enough to catch momentum can outlast a single viral moment.

Tinashe's 11-year wait: patience paid off or industry too slow? One word.
